analysis:
The supplied units are head-text excerpts of CHANGELOG.md only, covering lines 1-232 and 233 onward. This is documentation, with no executable source in the supplied excerpts. No code, authorization, encryption, billing or availability logic changed in what I could see, so no concrete security regression is identifiable from these units.

The changelog describes security-relevant changes elsewhere in the PR whose implementing source was not supplied:
- Numbered goose Postgres schema migrations, including the advisory lock and the fail-closed baseline.
- Frozen legacy MDM cohort and /v1/enroll gating (TB-009, T-036, TB-011).
- App Attest required for base rewards and for owner routing (T-052..T-058).
- Removal of GET /v1/provider/earnings, which is the T-031 fix.
- Removal of POST /v1/telemetry/events.
- Attestation challenges now fail closed on a missing status_signature (TB-009, T-033).
- Removal of the Python-era wire fields.
- The raised minimum provider version floor.
- An SSD prefix-cache TTL raised from 15 to 30 minutes, recorded as a SEC-035 re-acceptance (T-041).
- A 750 GB/day SSD write budget.
- A Stripe refund clock-skew fix and a Global Payouts migration (TB-008).
- A referral rewards settlement, which is new billing surface.
- An admin-only Autopilot inventory report.
- An advisory PR review workflow that runs the trusted base revision.

These claims are unverified because the implementing source was not supplied. Reviewers of the actual code files should check the migration lock and baseline behavior, the cohort freeze, enrollment proof validation, the referral settlement atomicity, and whether the threat-model entries need updating. I make no finding on those from the changelog alone.

Coverage is limited to the changelog excerpts. Deeper review of the code files in the PR is warranted for these behaviors.
